problems.title: Pathwise uniqueness for the square-root rough-Heston variance equation
problems.statement:
Fix $H\in(0,1/2)$, $v_0>0$, $\nu>0$, and a Brownian motion $W$. Consider nonnegative continuous adapted solutions satisfying $\sup_{t\leq T}\mathbb E[V_t^p]<\infty$ for every finite $T$ and $p\geq1$, of

$$V_t=v_0+\frac{\nu}{\Gamma(H+1/2)}\int_0^t(t-s)^{H-1/2}\sqrt{V_s}\,dW_s.$$

If $V$ and $\widetilde V$ use the same Brownian motion and initial value on the same filtered probability space, must they be indistinguishable on every finite horizon? A proof or a counterexample settles this question. This is already a concrete case of rough Heston, with constant initial forward variance and zero mean reversion.
problems.background: Strong simulation and coupling arguments need control of solutions driven by the same noise, beyond determining their distribution.
known_results: Weak existence and uniqueness in law are available for this affine Volterra model.
Pathwise uniqueness holds after localizing away from zero; the square-root boundary is the difficulty.
For a singular kernel $(t-s)^{-\alpha}$, Prömel–Scheffels require diffusion Hölder exponent $\xi>1/[2(1-\alpha)]$. With $\alpha=1/2-H>0$, this excludes $\xi=1/2$.

sources.title: Forde–Gerhold–Smith, Small-time VIX smile and the stationary distribution for the Rough Heston model
sources.finding: Explicitly says pathwise uniqueness is unknown even for constant initial variance; distinguishes weak uniqueness and localization.

sources.title: Prömel–Scheffels, Pathwise uniqueness for singular stochastic Volterra equations with Hölder coefficients
sources.finding: The full regularity assumption is stronger than one-half Hölder for singular kernels; Remark 2.2 alone is not the theorem.

nearby_results_checked: Prömel–Scheffels does not cover the square-root exponent for H<1/2.
The August 2026 local stochastic rough-volatility filtering paper concerns conditional-density equations, not this pathwise-uniqueness theorem.
review.conclusion: No resolution of this scoped question was located. This is a dated literature assessment, not a proof of openness.

problems.title: Physical Stefan uniqueness when jumps accumulate at time zero
problems.statement:
Let $g\geq0$ be a bounded integrable density on $(0,\infty)$ and $B$ a standard Brownian motion. Define

$$X_t^x=x+B_t-\Lambda_t,\qquad \tau^x=\inf\{t\geq0:X_t^x\leq0\},\qquad
\Lambda_t=\int_0^\infty\mathbb P(\tau^x\leq t)g(x)\,dx.$$

Require $\Lambda$ to be nondecreasing and càdlàg and to obey the physical minimal-jump rule. Writing
$\mu_{t-}(A)=\int_0^\infty\mathbb P(\tau^x\geq t,\,X_{t-}^x\in A)g(x)\,dx$, this rule is
$\Delta\Lambda_t=\inf\{z>0:\mu_{t-}((0,z])<z\}$, with the corresponding initial rule.

Assume the initial rule gives no jump at zero and a finite global minimal physical solution $\underline\Lambda$ exists. In the remaining regime where $\Delta\underline\Lambda_{t_n}>0$ for some $t_n\downarrow0$, is the physical solution unique? Prove uniqueness in this regime or construct one admissible $g$ with two distinct physical solutions.
problems.background: The loss process models contagious defaults in a mean-field system; uniqueness determines whether the same initial balance-sheet distribution determines a single loss evolution.
known_results: Muñoz reduces global uniqueness to short-time uniqueness and rules out accumulation of jumps at positive times for integrable initial data.
Blore–Hambly Theorem 3.1 gives global uniqueness when the minimal solution is continuous on some (0, epsilon). Remark 3.9 isolates accumulation at zero as the remaining possible mechanism.
Uniqueness of a maximal weak solution in the separate free-target formulation is not, by itself, uniqueness among all physical solutions here.

sources.title: Blore–Hambly, A transform approach to the supercooled Stefan problem
sources.finding: Reduces possible nonuniqueness to jump accumulation at zero; does not prove that this mechanism produces nonuniqueness.

sources.title: Muñoz, Free boundary regularity and well-posedness of physical solutions to the supercooled Stefan problem
sources.finding: Regularity and local-to-global uniqueness for physical solutions.

sources.title: Chau–Kim–Murugan, Uniqueness of the maximal solution of the supercooled Stefan problem in 1D
sources.finding: A uniqueness result for a different specified solution class; not evidence that the stated physical-solution question is closed.

nearby_results_checked: The September 2026 transform result substantially narrows the older survey question.
Jump accumulation is necessary for possible nonuniqueness here, not a demonstrated counterexample.
review.conclusion: No resolution of this scoped question was located. This is a dated literature assessment, not a proof of openness.

problems.title: Relaxed equilibrium existence with action-dependent diffusion under time inconsistency
problems.statement:
Consider an infinite-horizon diffusion on $\mathbb R^d$ with compact action set $U$ and relaxed Markov policies $\pi(x,du)$. Its generator is

$$\mathcal L^\pi f(x)=\int_U\left[b(x,u)\cdot\nabla f(x)+\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}\big(a(x,u)D^2f(x)\big)\right]\pi(x,du),\qquad a=\sigma\sigma^\top.$$

The current self evaluates a policy by $J^\pi(x)=\mathbb E_x[\int_0^\infty\int_U r(s,X_s,u)\pi(X_s,du)\,ds]$, with non-exponential time dependence. An equilibrium permits no positive first-order gain from a deviation over $[0,\varepsilon]$ followed by the prescribed policy.

Extend the relaxed-equilibrium existence theory of Wang–Yu–Zhang–Zhou to covariance $a(x,u)$ that depends on the action. Retain compact controls, uniform ellipticity, coefficient regularity, reward integrability, and the quantitative hypotheses of their existence theorem in appropriate uniform-in-action form; state every additional restriction. The target is an existence and verification theorem for the controlled-diffusion EHJB system, without assuming its solution exists. Any obstruction should identify precisely which proposed extension fails.
problems.background: Portfolio allocations typically affect both drift and variance. An existence theory confined to drift control leaves out that feature.
known_results: Wang–Yu–Zhang–Zhou prove existence through vanishing entropy regularization for drift control and explicitly leave controlled diffusion to future work.
Huang–Yu–Zhang establish a convergent policy iteration for regularized drift-control problems and also explicitly leave controlled diffusion open.
Special solvable models and uniqueness under stronger hypotheses do not establish the requested general existence theorem.

sources.title: Wang–Yu–Zhang–Zhou, Equilibrium under Time-Inconsistency: A New Existence Theory by Vanishing Entropy Regularization
sources.locator: Section 2 opening; Assumptions 2.1–2.2; Section 4 existence and verification theorems
sources.finding: Proves results for action-independent diffusion and explicitly leaves action-dependent diffusion for future study.

sources.title: Huang–Yu–Zhang, Policy Iteration Achieves Regularized Equilibrium under Time Inconsistency

problems.title: Integrable Schrödinger potentials for continuum SPX/VIX calibration
problems.statement:
Work at zero rates with positive SPX levels $X,Y$ at dates separated by $\tau>0$ and a nonnegative VIX level $V$ observed together with $X$. Fix their three marginal laws and a reference law $R$ on $(X,V,Y)$. The feasible laws $Q$ obey those marginals and

$$\mathbb E_Q[Y\mid X,V]=X,\qquad
\mathbb E_Q[-(2/\tau)\log(Y/X)\mid X,V]=V^2.$$

For the entropy problem $\inf_Q H(Q\mid R)$, establish explicit hypotheses for continuous marginals under which a finite minimizer admits integrable dual potentials:

$$\log\frac{dQ_*}{dR}=f(X)+g(V)+h(Y)+\Delta(X,V)(Y-X)+\Gamma(X,V)\big[-(2/\tau)\log(Y/X)-V^2\big].$$

The static terms must be integrable under their respective marginals, with the dynamic terms admissible and integrable as required for the dual portfolio. Identify sufficient assumptions and their limits; finite-entropy feasibility alone is not asserted to suffice. The target concerns continuum marginal constraints, beyond a finite-grid multiplier calculation.
problems.background: These potentials justify the semistatic hedge and the dual calibration algorithm, not merely the existence of a calibrated probability law.
known_results: Nutz–Wiesel establish integrable potentials for a two-marginal martingale bridge under their assumptions, while explicitly identifying the additional SPX/VIX constraints as unresolved.
Joint SPX/VIX calibration itself is already achieved in the literature.
Recent global multi-maturity feasibility and memory-selection results address a different question from integrable attainment of this entropy dual.

sources.finding: Explicitly identifies first-principles existence of integrable potentials for joint SPX/VIX calibration as open.

problems.title: A semistatic FTAP for calibrated equivalent martingale measures with finite entropy
problems.statement:
Let $P$ be a reference probability on $\mathbb R^2$ with canonical prices $(X,Y)$ and let $\nu$ be an integrable prescribed law of $Y$, inferred from a full terminal call-price curve. Define

$$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}(\nu)=\{Q\sim P: Q_Y=\nu,\ \mathbb E_Q[Y\mid X]=X,\ H(Q\mid P)<\infty\}.$$

Give a necessary-and-sufficient criterion, formulated in terms of semistatic trading opportunities and their appropriate admissibility or closure, for $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}(\nu)\ne\varnothing$. A zero-cost semistatic payoff has the form
$h(X)(Y-X)+g(Y)-\int g\,d\nu$.

The criterion must distinguish equivalent from merely absolutely continuous measures, impose the entire terminal law, and account for finite relative entropy. Simply restating measure existence, or using the usual FTAP for a finite menu of options, does not answer this question.
problems.background: This would characterize when exact option calibration can stay equivalent to a physical model at finite information cost.
known_results: Nutz–Wiesel–Zhao assume nonemptiness of this class in (1.3), then prove the entropy-minimization and semistatic-utility results. They explicitly ask for a trading criterion for that assumption.
Non-closedness of semistatic payoffs is a central obstruction.
Pennanen–Perkkiö provide broad semistatic duality results with a finite set of statically traded derivatives; that does not directly impose a full terminal law.

sources.title: Nutz–Wiesel–Zhao, Martingale Schrödinger Bridges and Optimal Semistatic Portfolios

problems.title: Uniqueness of the one-period Gaussian Kyle equilibrium
problems.statement: In the one-period Kyle model with independent Gaussian fundamental value and noise demand, is the affine equilibrium unique among all Borel-measurable insider strategies satisfying optimality for every observed value?
problems.background: The older survey listed this as open. A newly located working paper reports a resolution.
known_results: Monteiro–Tourky report uniqueness without restricting insider strategies to affine ones.

sources.title: Monteiro–Tourky, The One-Period Gaussian Kyle Model Has Exactly One Equilibrium
sources.locator: ANU Working Paper 708, statement and abstract
sources.finding: Reports a resolution for all Borel-measurable strategies, with pointwise optimality; the proof has not been independently checked here.

nearby_results_checked: Continuous-time Kyle–Back uniqueness is a different question.
review.conclusion: Do not publish this as an unqualified open problem. Track the reported resolution and review status separately.
